### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **2** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 277275aa42c44979a5fbbf5b38b346ff3a835582` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `634b6c8ab0165b0f3d198696cbba8097cd44eef1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts + packages/spec/src/security/permission-form-label-first.test.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts (`PermissionSetSchema.label`, `.name`), packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (`FormFieldSchema.required`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`TYPE_TO_FORM`, the `/meta/types` entry), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/anchors.ts (the `permission` registration), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/createDerive.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/builtinComponents.tsx, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/{en,zh-CN,ja-JP,es-ES}.metadata-forms.generated.ts, .changeset/27864-permission-set-form-label-first.md. The cited code was read to judge the one `hits` file, not reviewed; the rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT (comment 6525072867).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of the `permission` metadata kind: unchanged — right.** `PermissionSetSchema` (permission.zod.ts, `name: SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`, `label: z.string().optional()`) is not in the diff. The `/meta/types` entry builds its JSON Schema from `getMetadataTypeSchema(singular)` through `toJsonSchemaSafe` and attaches `TYPE_TO_FORM[singular]` beside it (protocol.ts around line 8683); nothing folds a form row's `required` into the served schema's `required` array, so the served contract's accept set is where it was. The new test's last case pins the label-less parse green on the branch.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`: `permissionForm` (exported via `security/index.ts`, served via `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY.permission`) changes shape — right, and correctly declared.** The Identity section now reads `label` (required) then `name` (required), and the `name` help text changes. Row order and a `required` override are renderer-facing layout: `FormFieldSchema.required` is documented as `Required override` (view.zod.ts line 3586), and the one Console consumer announces it as a visual star plus `aria-required` (SchemaForm.tsx lines 1939–1948), deliberately not native `required`, so no submit is blocked by it. No key is added, removed or retyped.
- **Console create screen: Label now precedes Name — right, and the mechanism the PR names is the real one.** `permission` has `createFields: ['label', 'name']` and a `label` to `name` slugify rule with `untilUserEdits: true` (anchors.ts lines 413–416) but no custom `CreatePage` (builtinComponents.tsx registers only `EditPage: PermissionMatrixEditPage`), so create goes through the generic `ResourceEditPage`, which passes `createFieldList` to `SchemaForm` as `hiddenFields` (the complement) and `fieldOrder`. `fieldOrder` only drives the flat fallback (`orderKeys`, SchemaForm.tsx line 1220); when a served form exists, `SectionedSchemaForm` renders `s.fields` in authored order and never consults `fieldOrder`. Hence the served section order put Name first on screen, and reordering the section is the one spec-side change that fixes it. The `untilUserEdits` claim in the new code comment matches `useCreateDerive` (`respectTouched` + `markTouched` from the edit page's `onCreatePatch` path).
- **Edit screen: unaffected — right.** `PermissionMatrixEditPage` draws its own `perm-label` input (PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx line 1972) and does not render the served form, so existing label-less sets gain no star and no new refusal on edit.
- **i18n bundles: regenerated output, key order follows the registry walk — read, not judged.** CI `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check-i18n-bundles`) is green on this head.
- **No gate on `main` pins `name`-before-`label` anywhere.** `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts` reconciles key presence and tombstones, not row order or `required`; `metadata-form-declared-rows.pin.test.ts` pins two unrelated rows. Test Core and Test UI are green on the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch**, `@objectstack/platform-objects` **patch** — matches what the diff publishes. Per AGENTS.md the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — what an author can write to a permission set is unchanged (no key, value, requirement or default moves in `PermissionSetSchema`; a form row's `required` override is a renderer hint, not a tightened requirement on the authored body). The `platform-objects` patch is owed because the generated bundles are shipped source in a released package.

`Clause-②: no` — right: the diff declares no accept-set change and makes none (① first bullet). The line appears, line-initial, in both the PR body and the changeset body; `Check Changeset` and the `PR-body guards` check-run are both green on the head. The changeset's prose claims (Console fills `name` from the label; `PermissionSetSchema` unchanged) are both true in the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1, "house pattern refuted — 16 other forms list `name` first": **answered.** The card's Wanted names label-first for this form only, and the seat accepted that reading; the other forms are named in the PR's Acceptance notes and filed nowhere, which is the correct carrier (no repro, no ruling). Not this card's scope.
- Dev deviation 2, "file surface beyond the claim (platform-objects bundles + patch)": **answered.** The seat amended the claim in comment 6525072867; the bundles are regenerated output and the hand re-translations of the `name` help are read as consistent with the English source.
- Dev deviation 3, "platform-objects typecheck, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:dts-closure` not measured locally": **answered by the head's check-runs** — `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Build Core` all conclude success on `634b6c8ab0165b0f3d198696cbba8097cd44eef1`.
- Dev deviation 4, "no independent review run": **answered** — this record is that review.
- Dispatch constraint "no change to the permission-set object's accept set or to name derivation": **held** (① first and third bullets).
- PR body's open question, "whether `packages/spec/src` counts as a published schema face": **answered** — `reviewFace` returns `packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts` as `hits`; the seat's handoff named the same tier. This record is rendered at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report: empty. Nothing to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts`** — judged against the card's ruling (label first and required, `name` after it, derived from the label; no accept-set move) and its first consumer, the Console's generic create form.

Holds. The section reorder is the change that moves Label before Name on the real screen (① third bullet: `fieldOrder` does not reorder a sectioned form, so `createFields` alone could never have done it). `required: true` on `label` reaches the control as a star and `aria-required`, and the Console's slugify rule fills `name` from the label until the admin edits `name`, which is exactly what the new code comment and help text say. The new test pins the registry identity, the section order, the whole-form order, both `required` flags with a control, the help text, and the label-less parse — the card's second acceptance box. Nothing on `main` reads a metadata form row's `required` server-side, so the `Clause-②: no` reading in the code comment is true in the tree, not just in the PR body.

Attempts to break it, and what each found:

1. **Should-fix — the required star is advisory in the Console, and this is the first row in the registry where the override and the Zod disagree.** Every other `label` row marked `required: true` (agent, skill, tool, flow, field, position, email-template) sits over a `z.string()` that is itself required; `permission` is now the only form whose required override has no schema behind it. The Console honours a row's `required` as `aria-required` plus a star, by design not native `required`, and its client validation is advisory and reads the Zod (ResourceEditPage.tsx around lines 945–960), so an admin who leaves a starred Label empty and types a Name still saves a set with no human label — the business reason the card opened on. Within the dispatch's constraint (no accept-set move) and the `domain:spec` surface, this PR delivers the ceiling, and it says so plainly in the comment, the test docblock, the PR body and the changeset. But a star that Save ignores is itself the card's filing-gate ② state, so the gap wants a carrier: a `ui` card for "the metadata create form's Save refuses an empty row the served form marks required" (or a one-line note on #27864 that the acceptance's "required" is the layout flag by ruling). Not a must-fix: the hits file claims nothing false and the ruling forbade the only spec-side cure.
2. **Should-fix — the `name` help over-promises for non-Latin labels.** `slugify` strips everything outside `[a-z0-9]`, so a CJK label derives to the empty string, and `useCreateDerive` then clears `name` (createDerive.ts, "Empty derivations … just clear the target; the UI then knows to prompt for manual entry") — but no Console surface issues that prompt (no matching string in the metadata-admin views or the studio i18n namespace). The help now reads "Derived from the label when you create the set; snake_case", and the zh-CN and ja-JP bundles say the name is auto-generated from the display name — precisely the locales where the derivation never fires, leaving a starred, empty Name under a help text that says it was filled. Suggested wording for the source row: "Filled from the label when it can be spelled in snake_case; otherwise type it (snake_case)". The three hand translations would follow. Not a must-fix: the derivation does run, the claim is true for Latin labels (the card's measured scenario), and the non-Latin case degrades to the pre-PR behaviour plus a misleading hint.
3. **No break — edit path.** The matrix editor owns the edit screen and draws its own Label input, so existing label-less sets (none in `examples/app-showcase`, whose two sets both carry labels) see no new star and no new refusal.
4. **No break — gates.** No gate on `main` reads form row order or a row's `required` against its Zod; the reconciliation gate's unchecked direction is key presence, not requiredness. Test Core, Test UI, Build & E2E UI and Spec property liveness are green on the head.
5. **No break — layout.** `columns: 2` with two `colSpan: 1` rows puts Label left and Name right on one row; the DOM order, which the whole-form test reads, is label then name.

Verdict on the file: no must-fix; two should-fixes (1 and 2 above), neither blocking.
